title: ～でございます — the very polite “to be”
summary: でございます is the very polite form of です. It is used by staff speaking to customers and in formal announcements. It attaches to a noun, and expresses ‘it is ～’ with respect to the listener.

patterns.gloss: noun + でございます (会議室でございます)

body.p: でございます replaces です in very polite speech. It is a form of 敬語 (keigo), used mainly by service staff and in business. The meaning does not change: こちらが受付です → こちらが受付でございます.
Shops, hotels, restaurants, phone calls and announcements: 本日は休みでございます (we are closed today). You do not need to use it yourself in daily life; です is enough.
The question form is でございますか. The negative is ではございません. Note that ございます is also used in greetings (おはようございます), but there it is a different use.

examples.ja: こちらが会議室（かいぎしつ）でございます。
あちらが受付（うけつけ）でございます。
examples.tr: That over there is the reception desk.
examples.note: あちら is the polite form of あそこ.

examples.ja: 本日（ほんじつ）は休（やす）みでございます。
examples.note: 本日 is the formal word for 今日.

pitfalls: Don't use it about yourself in casual situations; it sounds too stiff. Use です.
It replaces です only; the rest of the sentence stays normal.
